snippets.description: The accrual hook. `wrote_graph` gates the call, so a credit is only ever minted for a graph write that actually executed and committed. This is the money-surface guard: the pre-fix design called record_contribution unconditionally after _upsert_beam_identity, which returned None and silently no-oped on three separate paths.
snippets.content:
wrote_graph = await self._upsert_beam_identity(visitor, data, provider)
# ── Identity co-op: credit only a graph write that really happened ──
if wrote_graph and settings.identity_coop_enabled:
    from apps.api.services.identity_coop import maybe_record_contribution
    await maybe_record_contribution(self.db, visitor, data, provider)

snippets.description: The D-A signature change and its complete four-return edit set. `-> bool` at 1270; `return False` at the missing fingerprint/email guard (1275); `return False` at the combined do_not_resolve / GRAPH_WRITE_BLOCKING_SCOPES erasure guard (1289); `return True` immediately after the successful commit (1332); `return False` in the except path (1336, which previously fell through to an implicit None). Guard logic and ordering are UNCHANGED — only the returned value was added.
snippets.content:
async def _upsert_beam_identity(self, visitor, data, provider) -> bool:
    ...
    if not fp or not email:
        return False        # 1275
    ...
    if getattr(visitor, "do_not_resolve", False) or await is_email_suppressed_any(
        self.db, email, GRAPH_WRITE_BLOCKING_SCOPES):
        logger.info("graph_write_blocked", ...)
        return False        # 1289
    try:
        ...
        await self.db.commit()
        return True         # 1332
    except Exception as exc:
        await self.db.rollback()
        return False        # 1336

snippets.description: The three accrual gates. Gate 1 is merge-awareness (ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING on the per-day audit key). Gate 2 is the fraud gate covering BOTH is_abuse_flagged and is_bot_suspect. Gate 3 is the once-per-identity accrual rule, enforced by catching the partial unique index's IntegrityError rather than by a hand-rolled pre-check, so a concurrent race cannot double-credit.

D-B enforcement by absence. This module imports NO suppression symbol and re-lists NO scope literal, so the single source of truth for who may be written to the graph stays inside the resolver's own write boundary. Consequence: a blocked graph write produces no co-op row at all, which is what makes the co-op tables' absence from ERASURE_TARGETS harmless instead of a privacy hole. Asserted by an AST-based tripwire test.

ERASURE_TARGETS is unchanged by this phase. The co-op tables are deliberately NOT added to it (umbrella line 94 forbids this program from changing SPEC A's mechanics); the privacy invariant is upheld by never creating a row instead.

AC-10 acceptance guard. Turning contribution_enabled ON requires a 64-char lowercase hex terms_version equal to the pinned settings.coop_terms_version (422 otherwise), and record_consent_acceptance runs before the single `await db.commit()` at line 370 — so the acceptance row and the flag flip share ONE transaction and 'flag ON with no audit row' is unreachable. Turning it OFF is unconditional by design: opting out of a data co-op must never be gated.

Multi-tenancy is inherited, not re-implemented: verify_site_access returns 404 (never 403) for a foreign or unknown site_id, so the new flag surface cannot be used as an existence oracle. Proven by test_foreign_site_is_404_not_403.

Five settings, all default OFF/inert, with the required rollout order documented inline (erasure LIVE → migrations applied → legal review + re-pin digest → global flag → per-site flag via the API only). This is the production-exposure guard: as shipped, the accrual path is unreachable.

identity_coop_enabled: bool = False
coop_credit_per_contribution: int = 1
coop_credit_expiry_days: int = 90
coop_credit_hold_hours: int = 24
coop_terms_version: str = "c655274f585ef9b515688e9d4572f7cd64b8ed2fed8ebe6602e0040ecf73d7eb"

snippets.description: The two DISTINCT uniqueness rules. uq_coop_contrib_site_email_day is the per-day AUDIT key (AC-3 merge-awareness). uq_coop_accrued_site_email is a PARTIAL unique index — the ACCRUAL key (D-E). The partial predicate is load-bearing: a plain unique index would wrongly reject the later-day audit row the design deliberately keeps.
snippets.content:
sa.UniqueConstraint("site_id", "email_bidx", "contributed_on", name="uq_coop_contrib_site_email_day")
op.create_index("uq_coop_accrued_site_email", "identity_contribution_events",
    ["site_id", "email_bidx"], unique=True, postgresql_where=sa.text("accrued IS TRUE"))

snippets.description: Blind-index-only discipline. The event table has email_bidx and NO email / email_ciphertext column, so there is no decrypt path out of the co-op tables by construction. Asserted by test_contribution_event_carries_blind_index_only.

D-D: site_id-scoped with NO user_id column. site_id is the attribution unit and matches beam_identity_graph.source_site_id; user_id is always derivable via Site.user_id, so storing it would be denormalized state that goes stale if a site is reassigned. Phase 2 must aggregate across a user's sites at gate time instead of adding a column to this frozen schema.
snippets.content:
